brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#0 hex-acc-keyhole on piece:0,0,0;full allows wall hanging; build is vertical face with cover:0,0,0;full;top as clock dial

Built hexagonal clock face using cover as dial with two pencil props as hands positioned at different angles (prop:1, prop:2). Static representation readable as ~3 o'clock but no numerals/marks and not accurate - uses staging props not printed clock mechanism

requirements.requirement: Hands that turn and tell time (functional movement)
requirements.evidence: Configurator only checks fit/collisions and prints static plastic parts. No clock mechanism, motor, or moving hands are in catalog. The pencils are static props placed on surface and do not turn automatically; no timekeeping function. Material/process limits per rules mean electromechanical timekeeping is outside Hex Cluster capability.

finish.summary: Built a wall-mountable hexagonal clock form (single cell base + cover dial + keyhole accessory) with two pencil props posed as hour/minute hands to suggest a clock face. Fully functional turning hands that keep time cannot be built in Hex Cluster - it only produces static 3D-printed plastic parts with no movement mechanism, so that requirement is unmet. The visual representation is partial.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
